title: A miss tells you where to look
hook: Must a search ever step back?

knows: searching a text for a word by sliding the word along it
doesNotKnow: that a mismatch already tells you where the next match could start

misconception: After a mismatch you have to move one letter on and re-read from there.
objective: The learner can explain that after a mismatch the part that matched is known text, so the pattern can slide by its fallback table and the text arrow never moves back, which finds AAAB in AAAAAAAAB in 14 comparisons against 24.

claims.text: Searching for AAAB in AAAAAAAAB by restarting one letter on after each mismatch takes 24 letter comparisons (shown on the stage when both searches run to the end).
claims.source: Builder's node script: alignments 0..5, each reading the pattern until a miss or a full match, 4 comparisons each (the pattern's B meets an A for alignments 0 to 4; alignment 5 matches), 6 x 4 = 24. Counting rule: every comparison of one text letter with one pattern letter counts 1, matching or not. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 19): Own node script (scratchpad fc19b2/kmp.mjs, own naive search): alignments 0-5 at 4 comparisons each = 24; match at offset 5. | REOPENED 2026-10-14 (v3, wave D r5 revision by demo-builder): learner-visible sentence changed; needs a fresh check.

claims.text: Reusing what matched (KMP) finds AAAB in AAAAAAAAB at comparison 14, with the text arrow moving back 0 times.
claims.source: Builder's node script: standard KMP (text index i, pattern index j, on a miss j = fail[j-1], i unchanged unless j = 0). Compared text/pattern positions: 0/0 1/1 2/2 3/3x 3/2 4/3x 4/2 5/3x 5/2 6/3x 6/2 7/3x 7/2 8/3 = 14 comparisons, 0 back moves. Same counting rule as claim 1. KMP agrees with indexOf on 20,000 random binary strings. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 19): Own KMP (CLRS-style prefix function, written independently): trace 0/0 1/1 2/2 3/3x 3/2 4/3x 4/2 5/3x 5/2 6/3x 6/2 7/3x 7/2 8/3 = 14, found at 5, 0 back moves; agrees with indexOf on 50,000 random binary cases. Matches Demo.tsx KMP loop. | REOPENED 2026-10-14 (v3, wave D r5 revision by demo-builder): learner-visible sentence changed; needs a fresh check.

claims.text: The numbers under AAAB, 0 1 2 0, are its fallback table: after a miss following a letter, they say how many of the matched letters still match (stage label: 'A's kept after a miss').
claims.source: Builder's node script: standard failure function (length of longest proper prefix that is also a suffix) of AAAB = 0 1 2 0. Knuth, Morris, Pratt 1977; CLRS 4th ed. section 32.4. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 19): Own prefix function of AAAB = 0 1 2 0 (and by hand: A, AA, AAA have borders 0, 1, 2; AAAB has none). Matches FAIL in Demo.tsx and the reveal text. | REOPENED 2026-10-14 (v3, wave D r5 revision by demo-builder): learner-visible sentence changed; needs a fresh check.

claims.text: Both searches miss for the first time on comparison 4, when the pattern's B meets an A.
claims.source: Builder's node script: first failed comparison is number 4 in both traces (text letter 3 against pattern letter 3). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 19): Own traces: first false comparison is number 4 in both (text 3 vs pattern 3, A vs B).

claims.text: Restarting one on moves its text arrow back 5 times in its 24 comparisons (1 time after 5 comparisons, 3 after 14), re-reading A's it had already matched; the reuse search moves it back 0 times.
claims.source: Builder's node script: a back move is a comparison whose text index is lower than the previous one's. Naive after 5: 1; after 14: 3; after 24: 5. KMP trace: 0. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 19): Own traces, back move = text index lower than previous comparison's: naive 1/3/5 after 5/14/24; KMP 0. Same definition as backs() in Demo.tsx. | REOPENED 2026-10-14 (v3, wave D r5 revision by demo-builder): learner-visible sentence changed; needs a fresh check.

claims.text: KMP makes fewer than 2 x (text length) comparisons, and the text arrow only moves right.
claims.source: Knuth, Morris, Pratt 1977, SIAM J. Comput.; CLRS 4th ed. section 32.4 (O(n + m) matching). Builder's node check over 20,000 random binary texts (length 1-20) and patterns (length 1-5): maximum comparisons / text length 1.89, never above 2; this run: 14 comparisons < 2 x 9 = 18. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 19): Derivation: potential 2i - j rises by at least 1 per comparison (match: +1; miss with j>0: j drops; miss at j=0: +2), is 0 at start and at most 2n - j at the end, and equality would need j=0 at the end with every step +1, impossible since the last step is then a j=0 miss (+2) or a match ending with j=M>0; so comparisons < 2n. Text index never decreases by construction. Own random check (50,000 cases, n<=30, m<=6): max ratio 1.92, never >= 2, never a back move. KMP 1977 / CLRS 4e 32.4 not opened (from memory; bound re-derived).

claims.text: Every miss in the reuse search comes after AAA has matched; the table's 2 under the third A keeps two A's, so the pattern slides one place and the next comparison is the same text letter: 3 + 2 × 5 + 1 = 14 comparisons.
claims.source: Trace of KMP from Demo.tsx: comparisons 1-3 match T[0..2]; for i = 3..7 a miss (B vs A) then a match (P[2] vs T[i]) = 2 each, 5 rounds; then B matches T[8]: 3 + 10 + 1 = 14. Reveal paragraph 2. | Added 2026-10-14 (v3) by demo-builder.

recall.question: A search reads text letter by letter and, after a mismatch, uses a table of what the pattern matched so far. What happens to its text position?
options: It goes back to the start
recall.why: What matched is known text, so only the pattern slides; the text position stays or moves right, which keeps the total work linear.
